site.name: aurora-network
site.summary: Aurora Network — Privacy & Audience (local demo) Fictional social network. Local fixture for UXBench. Open `index.html` directly in a browser. Pages `index.html` — Privacy overview Entry hub. Four cards (Default audience, Tag review, Past post visibility, Muted words) link to each privacy-management surface. Below the cards, a "Snapshot" panel summarizes the user's current privacy state as a key/value list. `audience.html` — Default audience Radio-group selector with four options (Public, Friends, Custom list, Only me). Below the selector: dynamic explanation of who can see new posts, custom-list manager (create / inspect / view recent use), and a "Who can tag you?" radio block. `tag-review.html` — Pending tag queue

run_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore Aurora Network’s privacy settings experience, centered on the Privacy & Audience overview and the four linked management surfaces, while validating key state changes, destructive/recovery paths, and responsive usability.
run_plan.summary: Start from the Privacy & Audience overview to confirm the hub, cross-links, and snapshot framing of the privacy system. Then work through each linked page in order of user impact: default audience, tag review, past post visibility, and muted words, exercising visible controls and checking whether feedback, summaries, and navigation stay coherent. Reserve extra attention for bulk/destructive actions and pages with many controls, then repeat critical paths on mobile because the prescan already shows multiple undersized tap targets.
assumptions: The primary product area in scope is the privacy/settings section beginning at index.html, not the placeholder top-nav destinations that use # links.
All known functional pages are the five HTML files in the prescan: index.html, audience.html, tag-review.html, past-posts.html, and blocked-words.html.
Because this is a local demo fixture, some actions may update only local page state rather than persist across full-page navigation; persistence should be tested but not assumed.
The overview snapshot is intended to summarize privacy state and may reflect changes from deeper settings pages, especially the default audience link already pointing to audience.html.
risk_hotspots: index.html: snapshot panel 'Change' links may be ambiguous because at least one points to # while another goes to audience.html
index.html: overview cards and left-nav both link to the same privacy pages; check consistency of labels, counts, and destinations
audience.html: radio-group changes plus 'Save default'/'Discard changes' flow may have unsaved-state or misleading explanation issues
audience.html: 'Custom list…' option and custom-list manager ('+ New list', inspect/recent-use cues) are stateful and likely complex
audience.html: 'Who can tag you?' radio block may overlap conceptually with tag-review behavior and create policy confusion
tag-review.html: bulk actions 'Approve all' and 'Hide all' are high-impact and should be checked for confirmation, reversibility, and count updates
tag-review.html: per-item actions 'Approve', 'Hide tag', and 'Block user' are repeated controls with risk of accidental action or unclear aftermath
past-posts.html: 'Apply to visible' is a destructive bulk action tied to filters and selected target audience; validate scope clarity
past-posts.html: year/audience filters drive which posts are affected; check that visible-result logic matches action wording 'what you see is what gets changed'
blocked-words.html: add-word input plus Enter-to-save behavior may fail silently or create duplicate/validation edge cases
blocked-words.html: chip removal via × across 18 entries is repetitive and prone to accidental deletion without recovery
blocked-words.html: 'Import .txt' and 'Export .txt' are visible but may be stubbed in a local fixture; confirm behavior and error handling if any
All pages on mobile: many nav items and links were flagged as small tap targets in prescan

phases.title: Map the privacy hub and navigation model
phases.objective: Validate the overview page as the entry point, including card links, left-side privacy navigation, snapshot summary, and any directly actionable 'Change' links.
key_checks: Open each privacy destination from the overview cards: Default audience, Tag review, Past post visibility, Muted words
Compare left-nav privacy links against the card links to confirm they reach the same pages and use consistent naming/count cues
Inspect the 'Snapshot of your current privacy' section and test visible 'Change' links, noting which are actionable versus placeholder # links
Check whether overview copy correctly distinguishes new-post settings from retroactive controls such as Past post visibility
Record whether tag-review count ('7 pending') appears consistently in card and left-nav badge
exit_criteria: All overview-originating privacy links have been followed at least once
Any dead, placeholder, or inconsistent 'Change' links are identified with evidence
The relationship between overview summary content and deeper settings pages is understood before deeper interaction

phases.title: Exercise default audience and tagging preferences
phases.objective: Test the primary settings flow for choosing who can see new posts, including save/discard behavior, custom-list affordances, and adjacent tag-permission settings.
key_checks: Cycle through the four audience radio options: Public, Friends, Custom list…, Only me, observing helper/explanatory text changes
Use 'Save default' after changing audience and verify whether the selected state and any explanation remain stable
Use 'Discard changes' after making a different selection to confirm recovery to the prior state
Choose the 'Custom list…' path and inspect visible custom-list affordances including '+ New list' and the listed saved lists with recent-use metadata
Check whether selecting different audience options affects visible explanation text such as search-indexing implications or friend visibility wording
Exercise the 'Who can tag you?' radio block and note whether labels and resulting state are understandable alongside the separate Tag review page
Navigate back to the overview after a save, if possible, to see whether snapshot/default audience indicators update
exit_criteria: At least one successful save and one discard path have been attempted
All four audience options have been selected and observed
Custom-list management affordances and tag-permission controls have been inspected enough to assess discoverability and clarity

phases.title: Validate moderation queue actions in tag review
phases.objective: Assess single-item and bulk triage flows for pending tags, with emphasis on clarity of consequence, queue updates, and safe handling of higher-risk actions.
key_checks: Review the queue header and initial pending count ('7 tags waiting for review') against overview/nav badge counts
Use per-item actions on a sample of entries: Approve, Hide tag, and Block user, checking resulting item state/removal and any feedback
Inspect entries with additional context such as 'You don't follow this account' to see whether risk cues are prominent enough
Test one bulk action path ('Approve all' or 'Hide all') after first understanding whether confirmation or undo exists
Check whether action labels distinguish profile-linking effects from original-post visibility, matching the explanatory copy
Confirm whether counts update after individual or bulk actions and whether an empty-state appears when the queue is cleared
exit_criteria: All three per-item action types have been exercised on at least one item if enabled
One bulk action path has been explored with its aftermath documented
Queue count/update behavior and any confirmation/undo pattern are known

phases.title: Probe bulk visibility changes for past posts
phases.objective: Test the highest-risk retroactive privacy flow by combining filters with the 'Apply to visible' action and checking whether scope is transparent and recoverable.
key_checks: Inspect the timeline/year controls and the year select to understand how narrowing content works
Change audience filters (Any audience, Public only, Friends only, Only me) and verify that the visible post list matches the selected filter
Change the target audience select (Friends / Only me / Public) and confirm that it is clearly separated from the filter controls
Apply changes to a narrowed visible subset using 'Apply to visible' and watch for confirmation, warnings, or post-level updates
Compare the on-page instruction 'what you see is what gets changed' against actual behavior after filtering
Test whether individual post 'Edit' links are actionable or placeholders, and whether they support recovery or deeper inspection
exit_criteria: At least one filtered bulk-apply scenario has been executed
The distinction between filters and target audience has been validated
Any lack of confirmation, undo, or scope clarity for the bulk action is documented

phases.title: Stress muted words input and list management
phases.objective: Exercise the page with the highest control density by testing add/remove flows, scope messaging, duration/settings controls, and file-related affordances visible on the page.
key_checks: Add a new muted word/phrase using the text input and the visible Enter-to-save pattern, then verify it appears in the list
Try edge inputs such as duplicate phrase, hashtag phrase, and multi-word phrase if allowed by the UI, observing validation or silent failure
Remove one or more existing muted-word chips using the × affordance and check for immediate feedback or recovery
Inspect the 'Where do these apply?' section to verify the included/exempted surfaces are understandable and internally consistent
Exercise visible duration-related inputs/options on the page and observe whether scope/duration selections are clear
Test 'Import .txt' and 'Export .txt' controls to determine whether they trigger local demo behavior, no-op behavior, or browser file flows
Check whether the displayed total entry count changes when words are added or removed
exit_criteria: At least one add and one remove flow have been completed
Import/export affordances have been probed enough to characterize their behavior
The page’s scope messaging, count behavior, and control clarity have been assessed

phases.title: Repeat critical checks on mobile
phases.objective: Re-run the most important navigation and action paths in a mobile viewport, focusing on tap targets, density, wrapping, and whether high-risk controls remain usable.
key_checks: Verify mobile access to each privacy page from the overview and/or side navigation equivalent
Recheck known small tap-target areas from prescan: top nav items, left-nav privacy links, and overview card links
On audience.html, confirm radio options, save/discard buttons, and custom-list controls remain easy to tap and read
On tag-review.html, verify repeated per-item action buttons do not crowd or wrap into ambiguous groupings
On past-posts.html, confirm filters and the 'Apply to visible' control remain understandable without horizontal overflow or accidental activation
On blocked-words.html, verify chip list wrapping, delete × affordances, input usability, and import/export controls under smaller width
exit_criteria: Critical path pages have each been viewed on mobile
At least one key action per major page has been attempted on mobile
Mobile-specific usability findings are collected for navigation and high-risk controls

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 5 known HTML pages, with at least one return to index.html to compare overview state against deeper-page actions.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise most visible controls on each key page: overview links and snapshot links; all audience radio options plus save/discard and custom-list affordances; tag-review item and bulk actions; past-post filters plus one bulk apply; muted-word add/remove plus import/export and scope/duration controls.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat the overview navigation and at least one representative action on each of the four management pages in a mobile viewport, with special attention to prescan-reported small tap targets.

notes: Do not spend time on top-level nav destinations Home/Discover/Messages/Settings/Profile/Account/Email/Push beyond confirming they appear to be placeholder links if they remain # targets.
Prefer evidence-driven critique around privacy clarity, destructive-action safeguards, and consistency between overview summaries and page-level settings.
If actions do not persist across page reloads, still document the local interaction quality, feedback, and mismatch between expected persistence and observed behavior.

ux_notes: The click achieved the objective: blocked-words.html opened and clearly exposes the muted-word management surface, including an add-field with helper text, a visible count ('You have 18 entries'), existing removable chips, Import .txt / Export .txt buttons, scope checkboxes, and a duration selector.

The page is reasonably discoverable on desktop because the main controls are grouped under clear headings ('Muted words', 'Your muted words', 'Where do these apply?') and explanatory copy clarifies matching behavior ('case-insensitive', hashtags counted, exact phrase example).

Density is moderately high but still scan-friendly: 18 muted terms are shown as many compact chips in one block, which surfaces breadth of configuration but may become harder to scan/manage as the list grows.

There is some ambiguity in scope rules: the note says 'Some places (like DMs with friends) are exempted automatically' while 'Direct messages from friends' still appears as a checkbox option, which could make users unsure whether that channel is configurable or always exempt.

Small-target warnings indicate likely mobile usability risk for several navigation items (e.g. top nav heights 28–39px and sidebar rows 37px, below 44px guidance), though no desktop interaction failure occurred.

step.objective: Learn whether confirming mobile 'Approve all' produces clear feedback, removes or updates pending items, and keeps header/sidebar counts consistent after a high-impact action.
step.success_criteria: After tapping the modal's Approve all button, the page should show a changed queue state such as fewer/no items, updated counts, an empty/success state, or inconsistent aftermath that exposes UX issues.

ux_notes: Selecting the audience filter to 'Public only' achieved the promised WYSIWYG behavior on mobile: the page now shows '5 visible posts' and every visible post in the list is labeled 'Public', so the count and results appear coherent with the chosen filter.

The mobile filter controls support the mental model reasonably well because the updated count appears immediately adjacent to the filters and before the bulk action, reinforcing what will be affected by 'Apply to visible'.

Two mobile form controls involved in this task lack labels/aria-labels according to layout warnings (selects ux-9 and ux-10), which weakens accessibility and can reduce trust/clarity for users relying on assistive tech.
